description: Aggregator sources for the Best of the Internet obsession. The scout reads this file to find hunting grounds for hidden gems, and may append new sources it discovers. Each source is a URL or search pattern that tends to surface passionate, depth-first websites.

sources.notes: Meta-list of 'awesome' lists on GitHub — covers every niche imaginable
Marginalia Search — indie search engine that favors text-heavy, non-commercial sites
Wiby — search engine for the old web; surfaces handmade personal sites
Directory of active blogs organized by topic
Are.na — visual bookmarking for researchers and artists; deep rabbit holes
Show HN — people sharing what they built; filter for passion projects
MetaFilter — curated links from a community that values substance over clicks
Lobsters — invite-only tech link aggregator; less noise than HN
r/InternetIsBeautiful — dedicated to interesting, non-mainstream websites
r/DepthHub — long-form, in-depth content and discussion
Stumbled — StumbleUpon-style random discovery of small websites
href.cool — curated directory of weird and wonderful websites
Neal.fun — interactive visualizations and curiosity-driven projects (exemplar of the genre)
Personal Web directory — catalog of personal websites and digital gardens
Best of Show HN — curated archive of top Hacker News 'Show HN' posts by month and year
FOND/SOUND: deep-dive crate-digger blog by Diego Olivas with substantial Taiwan tag — long-form reviews of obscure Taiwanese, HK, Chinese records 1980s-90s.
Bandcamp Daily scene report on underground rock in Taipei — names specific bands, labels (White Wabbit Records), and albums across eras, useful as a hunting ground for Taiwanese music obsession
Mando Gap by Michael Hong — detailed critical rankings and essays on Mandopop albums by decade. Taiwan-focused, excellent for finding overlooked albums.
Xenharmonic Wiki — community encyclopedia of microtonal music theory and practice, active since 2005, covering tuning systems, composers, software tools, and scale mathematics.
Web Wanderings by Cloudhiker — monthly newsletter hand-picking unusual, non-commercial websites
Rogers Park Business Alliance events calendar — lists neighborhood-level Chicago events that often fly under mainstream radar, good for hyperlocal and community-driven programming

History Tools publishes well-researched narrative articles on historical places and cultural phenomena, with good depth on Finnish subjects — useful for design, architecture, and cultural history angles.
StoryStudio 故事 — Taiwanese history/culture site with a thorough deep-dive on Taiwan's banned-song (禁歌) history under martial law; recurring well for censorship-era music stories.

Chicago Race Riot of 1919 Commemoration Project — posts its annual free public history bike/trolley tour through Bronzeville and Bridgeport each July, plus related lectures and memorial events; good recurring source for under-the-radar Chicago history experiences.

Badewanne — 20-year Finnish volunteer tech-diving team documenting Gulf of Finland shipwrecks (17th century to WWII) with video and heritage-agency collaborations; source for maritime-history/hidden-gem Finland angles.
Chicago Honey Co-op class calendar — urban beekeeping nonprofit running recurring public hands-on classes through the growing season; recurring well for under-the-radar hands-on Chicago experiences.
Finland-focused travel blog with detailed, specific write-ups on villages, regional history, and hidden-gem day trips — good complement to historytools.org for lesser-known destinations.

Chicago Film Society's season calendar — recurring Sunday/Thursday screenings of rare 35mm/16mm archival prints (silent films, restorations, studio vault finds) at Music Box Theatre, Siskel Film Center, and Constellation. Good recurring source for under-the-radar preservation-themed cultural events with reliably dated listings.
Discogs 'Digs' editorial list, 'Nine Essential Records From Taiwan's Ambient History' — curated overview of Taiwanese ambient/new-age LPs (Chen Yang and peers).
Travel-focused site with detailed narrative articles on specific European destinations and infrastructure changes, including timely Finnish travel phenomena.
Chicago Ornithological Society's events calendar — recurring free beginner-friendly bird walks at sites across the city; good recurring source for under-the-radar nature happenings.

Volunteer-run wiki cataloging 7,000+ esoteric programming languages since 2005 (Rockstar, Piet, Shakespeare, Malbolge, Befunge), each with syntax examples and history. Good hunting ground for Best of the Internet gems.

Chicago Printers Guild's public calendar lists their rotating 'Books & Beats' park series (papermaking, letterpress, zine-making, live music) held at different Chicago Park District locations throughout summer/fall — free, all-ages, drop-in craft events that recur monthly at different parks.
National Repair Café directory listing Chicago-area chapters (Sulzer Library, Evanston, Aurora, Oak Park, Romeoville) with dates and locations — good recurring source for Chicago experiences beat.

Taipei Times runs a weekly 'Taiwan in Time' history feature covering forgotten figures and turning points in Taiwanese pop/folk music history (1930s Columbia Records era, campus folk, indigenous music).
Official site for the Bronzeville Art District's recurring 3rd-Friday trolley tour season (June-Sept) — a reliable recurring under-the-radar arts event, useful to check monthly.

Teleport City reviews obscure global pop/exploitation-adjacent music reissues, including deep dives on Asian disco/funk compilations like Taiwan Disco — useful hunting ground for forgotten regional pop scenes.

Chicago Botanic Garden's Garden Chef Series page — a running summer schedule of free chef demonstrations in the Regenstein Fruit & Vegetable Garden amphitheater, updated with specific chefs/restaurants and dates every second and fourth weekend.

A multi-part guide to Taiwan's shoegaze and dream-pop scene, profiling bands like I Mean Us, DoZzz, Manic Sheep, TuT, and U.TA — a useful crate for a genre largely absent from mainstream Mandopop coverage.

English-language blog run by a Lahti-based Finnish coach travel operator (est. 1957). Publishes practical, locally-grounded posts on Finnish seasonal phenomena, regional day trips, and winter travel logistics.
Chicago sustainable clothing swap collective; runs recurring 'Swap Social' pop-up events at bars/venues around the city, listed with dates and RSVP links.

A single hobbyist growing personal archive of interactive simulations recreating obsolete electromechanical and early computing systems (telephone switchboards, vintage minicomputers, etc.) — worth revisiting for future finds.

Illinois Mycological Association events calendar — public lectures on wild/edible fungi held at suburban Chicago libraries, plus members-only forays. Good recurring source for niche naturalist events with concrete dates and locations.

StoryStudio's comprehensive history of Taiwan's 898 banned songs under martial law (1949-1990s) — a rich hunting ground for specific banned-album/artist stories (Yang Tsu-chin, Lo Ta-yu, folk standards like 望春風, 雨夜花) distinct from reissue/genre-focused coverage.

Friends of Pullman National Historical Park events page — lists recurring free/low-cost public programs (walking tours, lectures, festivals) at the Pullman site on Chicago's South Side, updated regularly with dated Eventbrite listings.
Ye Olde Blogroll — a humanly curated (no algorithm) directory of ~1,300 independent personal blogs and sites, updated regularly. Good hunting ground for future internet-gem scouting.
Pure Person Press — Taiwanese-American label run by NTS DJ Angie QQ, releasing field-recording and vinyl-digging projects rooted in Taiwan; good recurring hunting ground for backstory-rich releases.

ibiblio is a UNC-Chapel Hill-hosted digital library and archive that has quietly hosted dozens of long-running solo passion projects (like the Lighthouse Directory) since the early web era — worth mining directly for more hidden gems.

Regional tourism site covering Karelia/eastern Finland's military history sites (Salpa Line, WWII trenches, border museums) — useful for Finland 'hidden gems' or regional-character angles beyond Helsinki/Lapland.

Chicago Full Moon Jam's schedule page lists free monthly fire-performance and drum-circle gatherings at rotating Chicago beaches, timed to the lunar calendar — a recurring under-the-radar event series.
